root_query: Has the US unemployment rate been lower in 2026 than it was in January 2023?
conclusion:
Has the US unemployment rate been lower in 2026 than it was in January 2023?

- [UNVERIFIED 0.00] What was the US unemployment rate in January 2023 (BLS CPS, seasonally adjusted)?: The provided evidence does not include the US unemployment rate for January 2023. Evidence [0] is BLS series LNS14000000 (CPS, seasonally adjusted) but only covers January 2024 through July 2026; evidence [1] is an unrelated World Bank indicator search. Therefore the question cannot be answered from the given evidence.
- [VERIFIED 0.90] What has been the lowest monthly US unemployment rate recorded during 2026 to date?: The evidence provided does not contain any data on US monthly unemployment rates in 2026 — item [0] is a World Bank indicator search returning unrelated indicator names (fertilizer consumption, agricultural land), and item [1] is court case records. Therefore the lowest 2026 US unemployment rate cannot be determined from this evidence.
- [VERIFIED 0.95] How does the January 2023 rate compare numerically with the minimum 2026 rate — is the 2026 value strictly lower?: The evidence provided contains no numeric rate values for January 2023 or for 2026 — item [0] is a World Bank indicator name search and item [1] is court opinion search results — so no numerical comparison can be made.
objections: The 'cannot be answered' verdict is an artifact of retrieval-window construction, not a genuine evidentiary dead end. Evidence [0] shows a successful call to api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data for seriesID LNS14000000 returning January 2024 through July 2026 — status REQUEST_SUCCEEDED in 82ms. The identical series contains January 2023 (the CPS seasonally adjusted series is continuous back to 1948); its absence reflects the startyear/endyear parameters chosen at fetch time, not data unavailability. Declaring the question unanswerable when one additional call to the already-proven-working endpoint with startyear=2023 returns the value mistakes a fetch-scope bug for an evidence gap.

Two of the three sub-questions were marked VERIFIED (0.90, 0.95) on grounds that 'the evidence does not contain any data on US monthly unemployment rates in 2026.' That rationale contradicts evidence [0], which lists all seven 2026 monthly values to date (Jan 4.3, Feb 4.4, Mar 4.3, Apr 4.3, May 4.3, Jun 4.2, Jul 4.1). The correct mechanism explaining these records is not 'evidence absent' but 'evidence misread' — the verification pass failed to bind the BLS payload to the 2026 questions, suggesting the pipeline's evidence-attribution step is unreliable here, which undermines confidence in the negative verdict itself.

Evidence already present undercuts any implicit suggestion the comparison could go either way or needs further investigation to be decisive: even without the January 2023 value, every 2026 observation in evidence [0] (minimum 4.1) sits far above the publicly known January 2023 CPS rate of 3.4 percent, and the series' own trajectory (3.7 in Jan 2024 rising to 4.1-4.4 through 2026) makes a 2026 value below the Jan 2023 level impossible on this data. The genuinely open item reduces to a single unfetched number from a source demonstrably reachable in the same session.
